# Write a mapper

You are writing a deterministic mapper from one source system's FOLIO record items into the consumer's app views in `in/views/views.d.ts`.

## What you have (all under `in/`)

- `in/schema/northgate-chart-v1.d.ts`: the source system's schema. This is the only documentation of the source.
  Its docstrings say what every field and code means; read all of it.
- `in/views/`: the target view definitions, written by the consumer. Their docstrings are the
  specification of the output: which rows to emit, which to leave out, units, statuses, time rules.
- `in/samples/`: 10 sample items from 2 patients of this source, in FOLIO Markdown form
  (frontmatter = envelope, then narrative, then the `json payload` block). `in/samples/samples.json` has
  the same items in JSON form, grouped by patient: that is the form your function receives.
- `in/harness/`: `sh in/harness/check.sh [asOf]` type-checks your mapper (strict, no Node/Bun types) and runs
  it on the sample patients, printing the rows.

## The task

Write `out/transform.ts` exporting

```ts
export function transform(items: FolioItem[], asOf: string): ViewRows
```

(the type `Transform` in `in/views/views.d.ts`). It receives every item this source
published for ONE patient, in no particular order, including items that were later superseded or
retracted, and a local date `asOf` (`YYYY-MM-DD`). It returns the rows describing this source's record
as of the end of that day.

Your mapper will be run, unchanged, on many other patients of this source whose records contain
situations the samples do not show. Rely on the schema's documentation for those, not only on the
samples. Nobody will review the output by hand; a mapper that runs cleanly but reads a field wrongly
produces wrong clinical data.

## Rules

- `out/transform.ts` is self-contained TypeScript. Its only allowed import is
  `import type { … } from "../in/views/views"` (and `"../in/views/views"`). No other imports.
- Deterministic: no clock (`Date.now()`, `new Date()` without an argument), no randomness, no network, no
  file system, no environment. Parsing dates with `Date.parse`/`new Date(string)` and `Intl` time-zone
  formatting are fine.
- It must type-check (`sh in/harness/check.sh`) and must not throw on input it does not expect: skip
  what it cannot read.
- You may write and run your own tests or scratch scripts under `out/` with `bun`. Only

content.text:
I've written `out/transform.ts`. It passes the harness type-check, the sample patients come out as I'd expect, and a scratch test of cases the samples don't show (hold, outside brand-name drug, weekly sig, eGFR race variants, platelets, urine creatinine, CKD restaging, removed or resolved problems, the end-of-day cutoff in Chicago) gave the expected results. For the second sample patient it returns empty lists, since that patient only has a referral and a list review.

Judgment calls:

- **Which items count:** an item is in scope if its `recorded` time, converted to Chicago, falls on or before `asOf`. Any item named in another in-scope item's `supersedes` or `retracts` (or in a void's `voided_items`) is dropped, whatever the void reason. I took the rule literally: a void that is itself voided doesn't bring the original item back.
- **Medications:**
  - I replay events per `med_id` in `effective` order. The latest event sets the status: start, change or resume is active, hold is held, stop is stopped. A hold never expires, and `review_on` is ignored.
  - For active lines, `status_since` is the date of the latest start or resume; for held and stopped lines it's the hold or stop date.
  - The ingredient comes from the start of the drug name, with salt words removed and a small brand-name table ("Jardiance" becomes empagliflozin). When two lines share an ingredient, the one with the latest event wins.
  - `rxnorm_ingredient` is never filled in: Northgate only gives product-level RxNorm codes.
  - Lines restricted as behavioral health (BH) are kept, since an item that was published counts as shared.
  - A frequency of `OTHER` becomes `QW` only when the sig says weekly; otherwise it's `other`.
- **Problems:**
  - "Resolve" makes a line resolved, "remove" drops it, and "update" keeps the current status. Fields come from the latest event.
  - Lines with the same ICD-10 code are merged.
  - Drug adverse-effect T-codes are left off the problem list. I don't turn them into allergy rows, because their wording doesn't name a substance.
  - CKD stage and albuminuria come from the description first, then the code (N18.31 is G3a). They are never worked out from lab values.
  - Billing and referral diagnoses are not treated as problems.
- **Allergies:** an inactivated line is dropped. I trust the clinician's `reaction_type`, and `severity` is used as the criticality.
- **Labs:**
  - Results are grouped by accession and component; I keep the copy with the most advanced status (corrected, then final, then preliminary). If that copy isn't a number (for example "Result invalidated"), the result is dropped.
  - Tests are matched by LOINC code, then Northgate's code, then the test name. Urine and point-of-care glucose are left out.
  - Platelet and white-cell counts in cells/uL are divided by 1000. A result whose unit isn't recognized is skipped rather than guessed.
  - The eGFR equation is taken from the lab comment first, then the test name, then Lakeview's code.
  - The race-coefficient eGFR is dropped only when the same specimen also has a race-free version. Spotting it relies on my guess that a trailing A or N on codes like `LK-EGFR09A` means "African American" or "non-African American"; the schema doesn't say.
- **Vitals:** each vital set becomes one clinic row, timed by its `effective` in Chicago time, with the repeat BP on the same row. Weight is converted to kg and rounded to one decimal. Temperature, SpO2 and height have no place in the view and are dropped.

My scratch test is in `out/scratch/t.ts`; only `out/transform.ts` is used.
